newsitem.title: GERMANY: Little hope for Bund gains as confusion reigns.
newsitem.headline: Little hope for Bund gains as confusion reigns.

text.p: Bund futures on the DTB succumbed to pressure on Friday, catching up with losses in London on Thursday when the German market was closed.

Traders said the air in the market was one of total confusion, offering few prospects for debt prices to gain ground as Bonn coninued to battle with the Bundesbank over plans to revalue currency and gold reserves.

"The total picture is completely confusing for the market, and when you get this kind of situation, markets invariably head lower," said Norman Beauchamp, head of derivatives at Cooperative Bank in London.

By 1454 GMT, the DTB June future was 18 ticks lower on the day at 100.71, tracking the LIFFE June future which was at 100.72, up 26 ticks on the day. The 10-year benchmark Bund was quoted at 100.48 for a bid yield of 5.928 percent.
Analysts said hefty gains in the U.S. were helping the market for now, but would not be able to brush away the gloom of domestic EMU worries.
The Bundesbank continued to hit back at the government over reserve revaluation plans on Friday, with Reimut Jochimsen saying the plans would hamper the central bank's movements in the run up to EMU.

Analysts said infighting in Germany, coupled with the prospect of a left-wing French government if socialists win he second round of voting on Sunday, meant markets were increasingly sceptical about the strength of a future single currency, with some players doubting whether the project will get off the ground at all.
"People just don't know. One minute you've got politicians saying yes it will go ahead, but then when you really look at the situation, you wonder who its all going to go through," said Beauchamp.
On spreads, Bunds lost out to Treasuries over the session, slimming the 10-year yield gap to 90 basis points from 94 at Thursday's close.
Analysts said this was a reflection of how strong an influence EMU concerns were having on the German market.

"That fact that Bunds only pratically managed to follow Treasuries higher this afternoon reflects the serious European concerns which for now remain a drag," said one. "This should stay a bearish influence next week."
